scenes.heading: Atoms do not stay alone
scenes.narration: Atoms rarely sit alone. Left by themselves most of them are restless, and joining up with a neighbour is the quickest way out of that restlessness.

scenes.heading: Sharing, not giving
scenes.narration: Neither atom hands an electron over. Instead both push one into the space between them, and that shared pair now counts towards the outer shell of each atom.

scenes.heading: Lower energy means stable
scenes.narration: But why bother at all? Because the joined arrangement sits at lower energy than two lonely atoms, and anything at lower energy is simply more stable.

scenes.heading: The balance point
scenes.narration: Push the two nuclei too close and they shove each other away. Let them drift apart and the pull fades. The bond settles exactly where those two effects balance.

scenes.heading: Where you meet them
scenes.narration: Water and methane are built this way, and so is the oxygen you are breathing right now. Every one of them is held together by shared electron pairs.

points: Electrons are shared, never given away
The shared pair fills both outer shells
Lower energy means a stable arrangement
